facts.raw_span: An 8-year-old girl was evaluated for recurrent seizures
left-sided weakness
developmental delays
Seizures began at age 3 months
no family history of neurological disorders
significant cognitive impairment
marked left hemiparesis with brisk reflexes
Electroencephalography showed focal abnormal brain activity
Brain magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated marked asymmetry of the cerebral hemispheres
significant atrophy of the right cerebral hemisphere
areas of cystic encephalomalacia surrounded by gliosis
suggesting a remote focal brain injury

concepts.why: The patient's left-sided weakness, significant cognitive impairment, and marked hemispheric asymmetry with atrophy are consistent with a hemispheric stroke.
The patient's seizures beginning at age 3 months and the presence of cystic encephalomalacia surrounded by gliosis suggest a perinatal stroke.
The patient's developmental delays, significant cognitive impairment, and marked left hemiparesis are consistent with cerebral palsy.
The patient's cerebral hemispheric asymmetry, atrophy, and areas of cystic encephalomalacia surrounded by gliosis are consistent with Sturge-Weber syndrome.
The patient's seizures, significant cognitive impairment, and focal abnormal brain activity are consistent with Rasmussen's encephalitis.
The patient's cerebral hemispheric asymmetry, atrophy, and areas of cystic encephalomalacia surrounded by gliosis are consistent with hemimegalencephaly.
The patient's areas of cystic encephalomalacia surrounded by gliosis are consistent with porencephaly.
The patient's cerebral hemispheric asymmetry, atrophy, and areas of cystic encephalomalacia surrounded by gliosis are consistent with schizencephaly.
